item.title: Elon Musk's Starlink and Starshield, and what they mean to Ukraine
item.description: Here's what to know about Starlink and Starshield, the technologies Ukraine is relying on in the war against Russia.

item.title: Chemical leak in Toledo forces evacuations, shelter-in-place
item.description: A massive chemical leak in Toledo, Ohio, is forcing some people out of their homes while others have been told to shelter in place.

item.title: Candidates clash over Trump policies, Senate control in debate
item.description: GOP Sen. Roger Marshall and Pastor Adam Hamilton debated tariffs, war and high fuel prices, and also addressed the most controversial issues in each of their campaigns.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers clash in final Michigan Senate debate
item.description: Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed clashed onstage Wednesday during the second debate in the increasingly bitter Michigan Senate race.

item.title: Judge curbs DHS efforts to conduct sweeps for possible noncitizen voters
item.description: A federal judge ruled DHS's practice of knocking on doors and asking people about their immigration status — and whether they have voted in recent elections — likely violates the Voting Rights Act.

item.title: On dating apps, men use AI to put their best face forward
item.description: How much AI is too much when it comes to finding love on the apps? "It's very subtle," one dating app user said of his AI-enhanced photos.

item.title: Son of Stephen Hubbard, American freed from Russian jail, speaks out
item.description: In an interview with CBS News after Stephen Hubbard was released from Russian custody, his son, Fr. Joseph Coleman, said his father might have made a mistake in staying in Ukraine when the war began.

item.title: The story behind the bug threatening up to 70% of the internet
item.description: Researchers at OpenAI have found a bug that puts up to 70% of the world's websites at risk. Robert McMillan, the reporter who broke the story for the Wall Street Journal, joins CBS News with the details.

item.title: Attack ad in Ohio governor's race sparks debate on how low is too low
item.description: A new campaign ad for Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy has sparked controversy and debate over what crosses the line in political advertising. The ad featured the estranged mother of his opponent, Democrat Amy Acton. Nancy Cordes has more details.

item.title: Stephen Hubbard's son after his release from Russian prison: "I want to embrace him"
item.description: Retired Michigan teacher Stephen Hubbard was a wrongfully held prisoner in Russia for more than four years before his release on Wednesday. Margaret Brennan reports on the details.

item.title: Childcare costs rising faster than rent, new research shows
item.description: U.S. families are struggling to afford childcare as costs rise faster than rent, with nearly 8% of households paying over $2,000 a month on daycare, nanny services and other programs. CBS News MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo has the story.

item.title: Man who halted runaway school bus: "It really shook me"
item.description: A quick-thinking bystander came to the rescue of the students and driver aboard a runaway school bus in Saint Paul, Minnesota.

item.title: First case of New World screwworm found in U.S. wildlife, USDA says
item.description: The New World screwworm was detected in an elk that was discovered on a game ranch in Pecos County, Texas.

item.title: Video shows moments leading up to police fatally shooting toddler
item.description: The Mississippi attorney general announced the police officer will not be charged in connection with the killing of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley.

item.title: Why "dump dinners" are going viral for solving some of the mess of family dinners
item.description: Two Arizona parents found a creative way to avoid the dishes and complaints from their kids. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: How "Grey's Anatomy" helped a quick-thinking hero halt a runaway school bus
item.description: A quick-thinking hero helped save everyone aboard a runaway Minnesota school bus when the driver experienced a medical emergency. Jonah Kaplan has the story.

item.title: What to expect from El-Sayed vs. Rogers Senate debate in Michigan
item.description: Michigan Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers are set to face off in their final debate before the midterms on Wednesday night. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has more details.

item.title: U.S. reducing troop footprint in Middle East, sources say
item.description: The U.S. military has been quietly reducing its footprint at posts in the Middle East due to ongoing regional threats from the Iran-backed Houthis and direct threats from Iran, sources tell CBS News.

item.title: Body cam video shows moments before Mississippi officer shot, killed one-year-old
item.description: Police body camera video posted by Darkhorse Press and verified by CBS News shows what happened moments before a Mississippi police officer shot and killed a one-year-old boy in pursuit of shoplifting suspects in a Walmart parking lot.

item.title: Former U.S. ambassador says Putin is a war criminal, calls Witkoff's comment "fatuous"
item.description: Former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine John Herbst joins "The Daily Report" to discuss Steve Witkoff's comment that Putin is a "humanitarian" following the release of an American citizen from a Russian prison.

item.title: Tennessee Titans cut defensive tackle Jordan Elliott after alleged gun incident
item.description: The head coach of the Tennessee Titans praised the character of defensive tackle Jordan Elliott after he was cut from the team on allegations he attempted to retrieve a gun after a fight during practice. Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: U.S. ordering some government staff to depart Saudi Arabia
item.description: The U.S. military has also been quietly reducing its footprint at posts in the Middle East due to regional threats from the Houthis and direct threats from Iran, CBS News has learned.

item.title: Vivek Ramaswamy under fire for attack ad featuring Amy Acton's mother
item.description: Ohio candidate for governor Vivek Ramaswamy is facing strong criticism for releasing an attack ad featuring his opponent Amy Acton's estranged mother. CBS News political director Fin Gómez has more.

item.title: Stephen Hubbard's son thanks Putin and Trump for father's release from Russian jail
item.description: Retired American teacher Stephen Hubbard has been released from a Russian jail after over four years of detention. His son, Joseph Coleman, spoke to CBS News about the good news. CBS News' Natalie Brand has more.

item.title: Witkoff blasted for calling Putin a "humanitarian"
item.description: After special envoy Steve Witkoff told Putin he was a "humanitarian" for releasing a U.S. citizen deemed to have been wrongfully detained, GOP Sen. John Cornyn responded, "No. Putin is a stone cold killer."

item.title: American Stephen Hubbard released by Russia, Trump confirms
item.description: Steve Witkoff lauded Vladimir Putin as "a humanitarian" as Russia freed Stephen Hubbard, an American deemed wrongfully detained by the U.S., after more than 4 years in prison.

item.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion to New Mexico in data privacy ruling
item.description: A jury found that the social media company had deceived consumers for years about its data privacy policies.

item.title: Armed federal agents knock on doors looking for noncitizen voters
item.description: Armed and in uniform, agents from the Department of Homeland Security have been knocking on doors to ask residents about their immigration status whether they're registered to vote.

item.title: Electricity bills force 1 in 5 to cut back on food, survey finds
item.description: Americans living on a fixed income are particularly vulnerable when electricity costs surge, a Consumer Reports expert says.
